 Zelda Pro Controller Restock: $99.99, Oct. 29 [2026]
 Tom Vance 
 Updated Oct 27, 2026 · 15 min read 
 Nintendo is scheduled to release the Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition on October 29, 2026. Nintendo’s official product listing is the place to confirm the price, and the Zelda edition is reportedly $99.99, which is a separate product from the standard Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller. Two days before launch, the Zelda Switch 2 Pro Controller restock question is already live. Target shows the controller as out of stock, Amazon UK marks it as temporarily out of stock, and Best Buy has a listing but no firm promise of units.

 That gap between a listed product and a buyable one is the story. Anniversary products have moved fast this month, and we covered the earlier Zelda 40th Anniversary Switch 2 restock pledge when it broke. The controller now faces the same demand pressure, with a much lower price of entry and a much bigger pool of buyers.
 This tracker lays out what each retailer listing says today, what Nintendo has confirmed, and what nobody has confirmed yet. Coverage of the controller from The Shortcut (Matt Swider), CNET, My Nintendo News and 9to5Toys points at the same set of listings. We separate hard facts from guesses throughout, because a restock date that nobody has announced is not a restock date.

 Add now What Nintendo Has Confirmed About the Zelda Controller
 The product carries a long official name: Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition. Nintendo lists the release date as October 29, 2026, which falls on a Thursday. The Zelda edition is reportedly $99.99, and the standard Switch 2 Pro Controller is a separate product, so check which price your cart shows. The design uses decorative patterns and illustrations inspired by The Legend of Zelda game series, and that is the full extent of the design detail Nintendo’s listing gives us.
 Nintendo has not published unit counts, per-customer limits or a restock calendar for the controller in anything we reviewed. The company has also not said how many units each retailer will receive. Nintendo reportedly confirmed that replenishment was planned for the Zelda anniversary hardware, including the Pro Controller, but did not announce specific U.S. restock dates or quantities. Those omissions matter more than the confirmed details, since they are the numbers that decide whether a buyer gets one on day one or waits weeks.

 It helps to keep the confirmed list short and exact. Name, date, price, Zelda-inspired artwork, and the existence of a second version with a display stand. Everything else in this article that sounds like a detail is either a retailer listing state or our analysis, and we label it that way.
 Two Versions, Two Sales Routes
 Nintendo is selling the anniversary controller in two forms. Each form follows a different path to a buyer, and a restock tracker has to watch both.
 The standard controller
 The controller on its own is the version major retailers list. Target and Best Buy both carry it at $99.99, which is also the reported price of the Zelda 40th Anniversary edition. The $89.99 price belongs to the standard Switch 2 Pro Controller, a different product. Amazon UK lists it too, though we have no confirmed price for that listing. If you want the controller without hunting through a specialty store, this is the version to track.
 The display-stand version
 The second product is titled Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller + display stand, The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition. It ships with a custom display stand featuring a map of Hyrule. Its price is reportedly $109.99 for the controller-and-stand package. The key restriction is availability. Nintendo lists this bundle as available only at Nintendo NEW YORK, Nintendo SAN FRANCISCO, and Nintendo Store. A second batch of the stand bundle was reportedly made available through Nintendo’s online shop, with shipping reported for February 2027.
 That restriction makes the display-stand bundle a different tracking problem. You cannot expect it to appear on Target or Best Buy, so watching those pages for the bundle wastes effort. The standard controller is the item that will show up in the big-box stock alerts.
 Retailer Listing Snapshot: Nintendo, Target, Best Buy, Amazon UK
 The table below records what each listing says as of October 27, 2026. We pulled the details from the listings themselves and from Nintendo’s product pages. A blank or “not confirmed” cell means our sources did not state it, so we did not fill it in.
 Retailer Listing Price shown Status on listing 
 Nintendo (standard) Switch 2 Pro Controller, Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition $99.99 regular price Release date October 29, 2026 
 Nintendo (display stand) Pro Controller + display stand, Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition $109.99 regular price Listed only at Nintendo NEW YORK, Nintendo SAN FRANCISCO, Nintendo Store 
 Target Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition $99.99 Marked “Out of Stock” 
 Best Buy Nintendo – Switch 2 Pro Controller, The Legend of Zelda, 40th Anniversary Edition – Multi (SKU 6691849) $99.99 Release date October 29, 2026, availability generally on release morning 
 Amazon UK Nintendo Switch 2 Pro-Controller The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition Not confirmed Marked “Temporarily out of stock” 
 Three of the five rows already show a sold-out or unavailable state before the product has launched. That pattern tells you the listings are placeholders for stock that has not yet landed, not evidence that stock sold out. The distinction affects how you read each label, and the next sections go retailer by retailer.
 Target’s $99.99 Listing and the “Out of Stock” Label
 Target’s page, titled Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition , lists the controller at $99.99 and marks it “Out of Stock.” That matches the reported price of the Zelda edition, so it is not a retailer markup. Target has not published a restock date on the listing as far as we can see.
 An out-of-stock label on an unreleased product is ambiguous. It can mean the retailer has not received inventory, or that it has loaded the product page early with zero units in the system. Retailers often build pages ahead of launch so that staff and systems are ready. The label alone does not say Target sold anything, and it does not say Target expects no stock on October 29.
 For a tracker, the useful Target signal is a change of state. If the page flips from “Out of Stock” to a buy button, a ship date or a pickup option, that is your cue. Anything short of that is noise. Until Target posts a date, we treat any restock timing as unconfirmed.
 Best Buy: SKU 6691849 and the Release-Morning Caveat
 Best Buy’s listing, Nintendo – Switch 2 Pro Controller – The Legend of Zelda – 40th Anniversary Edition – Multi , carries SKU 6691849. It shows a release date of October 29, 2026 and a price of $99.99, the same price Target uses and the reported price of the Zelda edition.
 The listing says availability is generally on the morning of release. Read that line carefully. It describes a general pattern for how the retailer handles launches, and it does not confirm that Best Buy will definitely restock or even stock on release morning. Treat it as a pattern, not a promise.
 The SKU is the most useful tracking detail here. Alert tools and manual searches both work better against a SKU than against a product name, since names get shortened and reordered across store pages. Keep 6691849 handy if you plan to check Best Buy by hand on Thursday morning.
 Amazon UK: “Temporarily Out of Stock”
 Amazon UK lists the controller as Nintendo Switch 2 Pro-Controller The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition and marks it “Temporarily out of stock.” The phrase “temporarily” implies Amazon expects units, but the listing gives no date. We do not have a confirmed price for the UK listing, so we do not compare it to the US figures.
 US readers should note that this is a UK storefront. It tells us the product is on Amazon’s radar in at least one region and that the retailer built a page for it. It does not tell us anything about Amazon’s US inventory or timing. If you shop in the US, treat the UK page as a weak hint about global demand, not as a signal about your own checkout.
 Amazon-specific advice carries over to every region. Check who sells the item before you pay. A listing sold by an unfamiliar third party at a high price is a different product from one sold or shipped by Amazon or by Nintendo’s authorized channels, even when the title matches.
 Nintendo’s Own Stores and the Display-Stand Exclusivity
 Nintendo says the display-stand version is available only at Nintendo NEW YORK, Nintendo SAN FRANCISCO, and Nintendo Store. That puts the company’s own retail footprint at the center of the bundle’s launch. Buyers who want the Hyrule map stand have to go through Nintendo directly, not through the big-box chains.

 Physical store access can come with its own rules. We reported on how the San Francisco location handled demand for the anniversary console in our piece on the Warp Pipe Pass requirement at the SF store , and readers planning an in-person visit should read that before they travel. Whether the same kind of access system applies to the controller bundle is not confirmed.
 Our reading is straightforward. Nintendo restricted the bundle to its own outlets, which gives it tight control over who gets the item and how fast it moves. That choice cuts competition from the large retailers for that specific SKU, but it also concentrates all demand onto three places. Expect those three to see the sharpest launch-day pressure.
 The $10 Price Gap: $89.99 at Nintendo vs $99.99 at Target and Best Buy
 The Zelda 40th Anniversary controller is reported at $99.99, and Target and Best Buy list it at $99.99 as well. The $89.99 price belongs to the standard Switch 2 Pro Controller, which is a different product. So the listings we reviewed show no gap that needs explaining. We can say what it means for a shopper.
 If both retailer listings go live at $99.99, a buyer pays the same at a major chain as the reported price for the Zelda edition. For a household that wants two, the cost is simply two controllers at that price. Weigh that against shipping, pickup convenience and any rewards you earn at the retailer. Our earlier cost comparison, PlayStation vs Xbox vs Nintendo ecosystem costs , shows how small accessory premiums add up across a console’s life.
 The more important point is that a $99.99 list price at a retailer is still a list price. It differs from a scalper markup. Treat a retailer’s $99.99 as a normal retail price and treat anything far above it on a marketplace as a resale premium.
 What Nintendo’s Latin America Executive Said About Replenishment
 The clearest on-record comments about Zelda anniversary shortages come from Bill van Zyll, Vice President and General Manager of Nintendo Latin America, as reported by GoNintendo and identified in that role in an October 2026 report. His remarks cover the Zelda 40th Anniversary products broadly, so treat them as context for the controller rather than a US retail schedule. On demand, he said: “We underestimated how well it would be received.”
 He described the problem as worldwide: “I will tell you that it’s a global phenomenon. We have this issue absolutely everywhere. We apologize for that.” That matters for a tracker. It suggests shortages are not isolated to one region or one retailer, which fits the out-of-stock labels now showing on both a US and a UK storefront.
 On replenishment, van Zyll said Nintendo was working on it: “We are working on replenishments of the special hardware and the software, but it’ll take a little bit of time. So I’m going to use this on you now: please be patient.” Asked about timing and quantities, he declined to give either: “I can’t tell you dates right now. We’re working on it. I can’t tell you quantities right now.” He added that the plan covers “the special controller, the hardware, the software.”
 Our analysis of those remarks is short. Nintendo has acknowledged the demand miss, named the special controller among the items in its replenishment plan, and refused to commit to dates or volumes. That is useful for setting expectations and useless for planning a purchase. Anyone claiming a precise restock date for the controller today is working without a source.
 Confirmed vs Unconfirmed: The Restock Fact Table
 Restock rumors travel faster than restocks. This table sorts the claims we could verify from the claims we could not, so you can judge any post or alert you see this week.

 The pattern is clean. Everything about the product itself is confirmed, and everything about timing is not. If a social post gives you an exact hour for a Target or Best Buy drop, ask for the source. We could not find one.
 How to Read Stock Signals Without Getting Burned
 A restock tracker is only as good as the signals it watches. The table below maps each label we have seen, plus the states you should expect next, to what the label actually tells you.
 Signal Seen where today What it tells you Your move 
 “Out of Stock” Target No units available to buy right now Check back on release day, watch for a state change 
 “Temporarily out of stock” Amazon UK Amazon expects units but gives no date Set a page alert, avoid third-party sellers 
 Release date shown, no stock promise Best Buy Product page exists, general launch-morning pattern Check Thursday morning using SKU 6691849 
 Store-restricted availability Nintendo display-stand listing Bundle sold only through Nintendo outlets Plan an official Nintendo store visit or order 
 Buy button, ship date or pickup option appears Not yet seen Retailer has loaded real inventory Buy promptly, quantities may be small 
 Price far above $99.99 on a marketplace Not yet confirmed Likely a resale premium, not retail Wait for retail restocks if you can 
 Two habits protect you. First, never pay a marketplace premium because a page says “only a few left,” since that wording can be written by anyone. Second, confirm the exact product title before you check out. The standard controller and the display-stand bundle share a name, and you want to know which one is in your cart.
 Historical Context: A Month of Zelda Anniversary Sellouts
 The controller launches into a crowded fortnight. Nintendo has stacked Zelda anniversary releases close together, and we tracked that run in Nintendo’s Switch 2 Zelda blitz of four launches in 14 days . Buyers who watched earlier items sell out now bring that memory to the controller, which raises the odds that demand shows up in the first hour.
 The hardware side of that run has already stressed supply. Our report on the Zelda Ocarina of Time release and the hardware sellout showed how quickly anniversary-branded gear disappears once a launch date arrives. Nintendo’s own Latin America executive has said the company underestimated how well the Zelda products would be received, which fits that history.
 The pattern is consistent. Limited-edition Nintendo accessories tied to a milestone tend to draw collectors as well as players, and collectors buy without the usual price sensitivity. A controller is cheaper than a console, so more people can afford to chase it. That combination explains why a limited-edition accessory can behave like a scarce item.
 Competitive Comparison: Which Route Gives the Best Odds?
 No route guarantees a controller, but the routes differ in price, certainty and effort. We rank them by what the listings support, not by what we hope will happen.
 Nintendo direct and Nintendo’s stores list the controller at $99.99 and are the only route to the display-stand bundle, reported at $109.99. They also concentrate demand, so competition for each unit is high. Best Buy pairs a $99.99 price with a clear SKU and a general release-morning availability pattern, which makes it the most trackable big-box option. Target also lists $99.99 but currently shows “Out of Stock” with no timing signal. Amazon UK gives the least actionable information for US buyers, since it lacks a confirmed price and sits in a different market.
 If you already own the console and a spare controller slot in your budget, the best plan is to watch two channels at once. Pair Nintendo’s official page with one big-box retailer, and set alerts on both. Players still choosing between bundles can read our comparison of Switch 2 bundles at $529.99 and $549.99 , and our gaming coverage hub collects the rest of this month’s Nintendo news.
 Five Predictions for the Controller After October 29
 These are our expectations, not reported facts. Nobody at Nintendo or the retailers has confirmed any of them.
 The standard controller will sell out at the major retailers within hours of its first in-stock window. Nintendo’s own acknowledgment that demand outran supply for other Zelda products makes a slow sell-through unlikely.
 Target and Best Buy will keep the $99.99 price instead of dropping toward $89.99. Retailer list prices rarely fall during a launch week for limited-edition items.
 Restocks will arrive without advance notice. Nintendo declined to give dates or quantities in its executive’s remarks, and retailers usually follow the supplier’s lead.
 The display-stand bundle will draw the heaviest pressure per unit, because only Nintendo NEW YORK, Nintendo SAN FRANCISCO and Nintendo Store carry it.
 Resale listings will appear above retail within the first week. Marketplace sellers tend to price limited Nintendo accessories well over list when retail stock runs dry.
 The first two predictions are the most likely. The last depends on how many units reach buyers, which no source has quantified. Check back after Thursday, since the listing states in the table above are the first things to change.
 Frequently Asked Questions
 When does the Zelda 40th Anniversary Switch 2 Pro Controller come out? Nintendo lists the release date as October 29, 2026. Both the standard controller and the display-stand version carry that date.
 How much does the Zelda Switch 2 Pro Controller cost? Nintendo has not confirmed a single regular price that covers both versions. The standard Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller and the Zelda 40th Anniversary edition, which is scheduled for release on October 29, 2026, are different products, so check Nintendo’s U.S. store and retailer listings for the price of each.
 Is there a confirmed restock date? No. Neither Nintendo nor the retailers we checked has published a restock date or time. The Nintendo Latin America executive quoted above declined to give dates or quantities.
 Will Best Buy restock on release morning? It is not confirmed. The Best Buy listing says availability is generally on the morning of release, which describes a typical pattern and does not guarantee stock.
 Why does Target say “Out of Stock”? The listing carries that label, and Target has not explained it. An early product page can show zero stock before inventory arrives, so the label does not by itself mean the controller sold out.
 Where can I buy the display-stand version? Nintendo lists it as available only at Nintendo NEW YORK, Nintendo SAN FRANCISCO, and Nintendo Store. It includes a custom display stand with a map of Hyrule.
 What is Best Buy’s SKU for the controller? The Best Buy listing uses SKU 6691849. Searching by SKU is more reliable than searching by product name.
